transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: Welcome to Shelf Life, the retail podcast. I'm Laura Chen, and today I have e-commerce consultant Victor Mensah and retail analyst Dana Price.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: Thanks Laura, great to be back.

transcript.speaker: Dana
transcript.text: Hi everyone, happy to be here.

transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: Let's start with the big picture. How big is online shopping, really?

transcript.speaker: Dana
transcript.text: Smaller than people assume. E-commerce is only about 16% of total US retail sales, according to the Census Bureau.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: Cyber Monday is roughly a $10 billion day for US online sales. That's the number every retailer plans around.

transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: What's the biggest headache for online stores?

transcript.speaker: Dana
transcript.text: Abandoned carts. About seven in ten online shopping carts never make it to checkout.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: We fixed a big chunk of that at one client. We cut their cart abandonment by a third just by adding Apple Pay at checkout.

transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: What about the new players, like Temu?

transcript.speaker: Dana
transcript.text: Temu is the one to watch. It's owned by Alibaba, which is how it can undercut everyone on price.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I think its growth is built on ad spend, not loyalty. When the ads stop, the customers go.

transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: So where do physical stores end up?

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: By 2030, most physical stores will be showrooms. You'll browse in person and the order will ship from a warehouse.

transcript.speaker: Dana
transcript.text: I disagree. People still love the in-store experience, and the best retailers are leaning into it.

transcript.speaker: Laura
transcript.text: A friendly disagreement to end on. Victor, Dana, thank you both for joining Shelf Life.
